evidence.excerpt: Semi-anechoic chambers of 3 m and 5 m class are widely used in Serbian and regional accredited testing laboratories, yet systematic multi-laboratory repeatability data for these facilities remain scarce. This study organised a proficiency test involving five laboratories in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, each measuring radiated emissions from two identical reference radiators—a broadband comb generator and a stabilised 868 MHz transmitter—over the range 30 MHz to 1 GHz. Between-laboratory standard deviation ranged from 1.9 dB to 4.7 dB depending on frequency and polarisation, with the largest deviations observed below 80 MHz where chamber resonances are most significant. Within-laboratory repeatability standard deviation remained below 1.2 dB for all participants. The 5 m chambers showed a systematic 1.3 dB lower variability index than 3 m chambers across the full frequency range. The paper discusses causes of between-laboratory dispersion and proposes a standardised reference radiator procedure for routine verification of chamber performance between formal ISO 17025 audits.
